nodes.name: Webhook: Follow-up Scheduled
nodes.notes: responseMode=onReceived acknowledges the scheduling request immediately (spec section 20) — the backend caller (FollowupService.schedule) never waits on this workflow's Wait node.

nodes.name: Validate & Normalize Payload
nodes.notes: event_id/followup_id, case_id, customer_id and a next-check timestamp must all be present; if a upi_reference_id is included it must be purely numeric. No business deadline math happens here — only presence/shape checks.

nodes.name: Invalid Payload - No-op
nodes.notes: Malformed payload — safe termination. No backend call is made.

nodes.name: Wait - Next Check
nodes.notes: Waits until the backend-supplied timestamp — never a hardcoded delay, never a T+1/T+5 calculation done here. Reused as-is for UPI, refund, bill, FASTag and AutoPay follow-ups; only the payload differs.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ followup_id: $('Webhook: Follow-up Scheduled').item.json.body.followup_id, event_id: $('Webhook: Follow-up Scheduled').item.json.body.event_id }) }}

nodes.name: Execute Follow-up - Backend
nodes.notes: The ONLY place a decision is made — the backend rechecks the transaction, re-evaluates the deterministic policy engine, and performs the action. Safe to retry: idempotent per followup_id, so a network failure after a real dispute-raise never raises a second one — a retry just returns the same outcome.

nodes.name: Switch - Resolved?
nodes.notes: First half of the 3-way Switch - Follow-up Outcome branch (RESOLVED / ACTION_TAKEN-ESCALATED / CONTINUE_MONITORING), built from two chained IF nodes for schema reliability. Branches on the backend's own `outcome` field — never recomputed here.

nodes.name: Switch - Action Taken or Escalated?
nodes.notes: Second half of the outcome switch. False output here means CONTINUE_MONITORING (the still-pending / not-yet-breached case).

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ case_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.case_id, customer_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.customer_id, event_id: $('Webhook: Follow-up Scheduled').item.json.body.event_id, correlation_id: $('Webhook: Follow-up Scheduled').item.json.body.correlation_id, workflow_id: $execution.id, result: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.result, outcome: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.outcome, action_taken: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.action_taken, current_compensation: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.current_compensation, next_check_at: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.next_check_at }) }}

nodes.name: Report Result - Backend (Resolved)
nodes.notes: Audit-only report — current_compensation and every other value here is forwarded verbatim from the backend's own response, never computed in n8n.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ case_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.case_id, customer_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.customer_id, notification_type: 'CASE_RESOLVED', message: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.notification_message }) }}

nodes.name: Notify Customer (Resolved)
nodes.notes: The message text is whatever /execute-followup already generated and sent — this call is dedup'd server-side on an exact (customer_id, case_id, message) match, so it can never double-notify even on retry.

nodes.name: Memory Recorded (Resolved)
nodes.notes: No action here by design (spec section 15): the backend's MemoryService already wrote the resolution event to Cognee inside /execute-followup, atomically with the decision. A second, independent n8n -> Cognee write would duplicate memory logic.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ case_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.case_id, customer_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.customer_id, event_id: $('Webhook: Follow-up Scheduled').item.json.body.event_id, correlation_id: $('Webhook: Follow-up Scheduled').item.json.body.correlation_id, workflow_id: $execution.id, result: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.result, outcome: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.outcome, action_taken: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.action_taken, current_compensation: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.current_compensation, next_check_at: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.next_check_at }) }}

nodes.name: Report Result - Backend (Action Taken)
nodes.notes: Covers DISPUTE_RAISED and ESCALATED. current_compensation is the backend/policy-engine value (e.g. 200) — n8n only forwards it, never calculates it.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ case_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.case_id, customer_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.customer_id, notification_type: 'CASE_UPDATE', message: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.notification_message }) }}

nodes.name: Notify Customer (Action Taken)
nodes.notes: e.g. "Your payment issue remained unresolved after the applicable resolution window. Nishchint has raised a dispute and will continue tracking it." — generated by the backend (LLM + verified facts only), not n8n.

nodes.name: Memory Recorded (Action Taken)
nodes.notes: Already written to Cognee by the backend's MemoryService during /execute-followup (remember_resolution). See the note on "Memory Recorded (Resolved)".

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ case_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.case_id, customer_id: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.customer_id, event_id: $('Webhook: Follow-up Scheduled').item.json.body.event_id, correlation_id: $('Webhook: Follow-up Scheduled').item.json.body.correlation_id, workflow_id: $execution.id, result: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.result, outcome: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.outcome, action_taken: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.action_taken, current_compensation: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.current_compensation, next_check_at: $('Execute Follow-up - Backend').item.json.next_check_at }) }}

nodes.name: Report Result - Backend (Monitoring)
nodes.notes: STILL_PENDING / CONTINUE_MONITORING. No customer notification for a routine not-yet-breached recheck — matches existing behavior.

nodes.name: Next Check Scheduled by Backend
nodes.notes: This execution ends here on purpose. The backend already scheduled the next Followup row (next_check_at above) and — via the SAME FollowupService.schedule() path that started this run — will fire a brand-new 'Follow-up Scheduled' webhook when it's time, starting a fresh, independent workflow execution. This avoids looping a single long-running n8n execution and keeps each run's idempotency key (followup_id/event_id) unambiguous. See n8n/README.md "How the autonomous loop continues".
